messages:
morgan: FYI found an IDOR on /api/v1/deployments/{id}/logs — non-admin can fetch other orgs' logs by guessing ids. posting quick repro. @jamie @devon
jamie: can you paste the curl + sample response? need to triage.
morgan: repro below:
```
# as normal user token
curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $USER_TOKEN\" \"https://app.redwood.ai/api/v1/deployments/987654321/logs\"
```
response (truncated):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"deployment_id":987654321,"org_id":"org-gns4","log_lines":["2026-03-18T12:01:02 main: starting","2026-03-18T12:03:10 auth: token=sk_live_***..."],"s3_path":"s3://redwood-logs/org-abc/987654321.log","presigned_url":"https://s3.aws/...X-Amz-Signature=..."}
```
jamie: ouch. that looks bad. is the endpoint supposed to be admin-only?
morgan: yes, only admins should access deployment logs. handler was missing an RBAC check after the refactor.
devon: I'm putting a temporary WAF rule to block GET /api/v1/deployments/*/logs from non-internal IPs now. can confirm once applied.
oncall-sre: applying rule (waf-rule-462) to block external traffic to that path.
sec-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026-0042 | P2 | "IDOR: deployment logs exposure" | created by morgan
jamie: plan for containment: 1) feature-flag disable logs endpoint public access 2) add strict RBAC check and unit tests 3) search for presigned urls in responses and rotate as needed. I'll start PR for the RBAC check.
devon: containment steps in progress: WAF rule applied at 1776001400, FF disable rolled at 1776001420. Confirmed previously accessible endpoint now returns 403 for test token.
morgan: thanks. scope: I scanned a small sample and found 3 distinct org_ids returned via guessed ids. need broader query.
devon: running query across request logs (range: 2026-03-16 to 2026-03-18) to count unique deployment_id hits returning 200 for non-admin tokens. ETA ~45m.
jamie: quick hotfix: adding `require_role("admin")` to the handler + integration tests. will canary 1% then increase. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1234
lee: product note: disable self-serve deployment log browsing for non-admins until permanent fix. also add RBAC gap to roadmap.
carmen: legal here — need to know if any logs contained secrets or full API keys. if so, we may need customer notifications and possibly data-protection notifications.
morgan: sample had truncated token fragments but not full keys. still need exhaustive check.
devon: search results: 38 unique deployment IDs accessed with non-admin tokens in the window. flagging which org_ids are affected and starting impact list.
jamie: checklist for follow-ups: - add audit logging for `GET /deployments/:id/logs` with requester_org and requester_role - reject request if requester_org != deployment.org - integration test asserting 403 for non-admins - monitor alert if >0 200s from non-admins
oncall-sre: audit log entry created for containment actions and WAF change.
sec-bot: INC-2026-0042 updated: containment in progress; owner=jamie; sla=P2.
carmen: please collate timeline and exact scope. I'll draft customer comms templates once we have the list.
morgan: noted. also need to check S3 object encryption: are logs encrypted with AWS KMS CMK or default SSE-S3? jamie/devon can check storage class & KMS key usage.
devon: S3 metadata shows SSE-KMS used for most buckets; a few older objects were SSE-S3. If presigned URL was exposed, SSE doesn't prevent read via the presigned url. rotation of signing keys might be required for presigned urls generated by our service. investigating who generated the presigned URLs and TTLs.
jamie: if presigned urls with long TTLs were returned, we should rotate and reduce TTLs to <5m by default. also enforce signed-url generation via service principal with restricted KMS access.
lee: confirm plan: short-term containment done; medium-term: RBAC + tests + audit logs; long-term: harden presigned URL policy + KMS key governance + alerting.
morgan: I'll open the postmortem and runbook update ticket. postmortem scheduled tomorrow 10:00 PT. owners: jamie (fix/PR), devon (scope + infra), carmen (legal/comms), lee (product decisions).
jamie: rolling out canary now. will post deploy timestamps and rollback steps in the ticket.
devon: confirmed no large-scale exfil pattern beyond log snippets so far. expanding search across the week.
carmen: legal will wait for final scope before sending notices. prepare draft language: what, when, affected org_ids, remediation steps.
sec-bot: INC-2026-0042 state=contained updated_at=1776001589
morgan: thanks everyone. please add any follow-ups to the ticket and I'll track until postmortem.
